subject: physics
question_text: Define average pressure. State its SI unit and dimensional formula. Is pressure a scalar or a vector quantity?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 1 (printed p.105). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: average pressure is P = F/A with SI unit N m⁻² (the pascal) and dimensional formula [ML⁻¹T⁻²]; pressure is a scalar because the force producing it always acts normal to the surface, whatever the surface's orientation, so no fixed direction attaches to pressure itself.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition, formula and unit
lines: SI unit N m⁻², also called the
steps.margin_note: First mark. Give the definition, the formula P = F/A, the SI unit and the dimensional formula.
steps.why: The definition names pressure as force per unit area, and the unit and dimensional formula are the standard way to state any physical quantity completely.
common_mistakes: Giving the formula alone without stating it in words as force per unit area.
Giving the unit without naming it as the pascal.

recall.must_convey: That average pressure is the normal force per unit area, P equals F over A, SI unit newton per metre squared or pascal, dimensional formula M L to the minus 1 T to the minus 2.

steps.memory_tip: Pressure is force spread over area: P = F/A, unit pascal.

steps.label: Pressure is a scalar quantity
lines: The force on a surface always acts
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say pressure is a scalar and give the reason: the force is always normal to the surface, whatever its orientation.
steps.why: At a point the fluid presses equally whichever way the surface faces, and the force's direction is fixed by the surface, not by the pressure, so pressure carries no direction of its own.
common_mistakes: Calling pressure a vector because the force producing it is a vector.
Saying pressure has no direction without giving the reason.

recall.must_convey: That pressure is a scalar because the force is always normal to the surface, whatever the surface's orientation.
accept: force is always normal to the surface

steps.memory_tip: The force is always normal to whichever surface it acts on, so pressure itself has no direction.

insider_note: Two marks: the definition with formula and unit, then the reason pressure is a scalar. The reason — force normal to the surface whatever its orientation — is the substance of the second mark, not just the word 'scalar' on its own.
